studies.name: Ahmed et al. — Teacher professional development for disability inclusion in low- and middle-income Asia-Pacific countries: An evidence and gap map
studies.draft_uses: 50 studies found; 16 of 41 countries report evidence on in-service TPD; Vietnam teachers reported training improved teaching quality; Malaysia special educators agreed technology-based practices improved professional knowledge; one-day workshop on Equality and Non-discrimination Module influenced students; no studies on supporting positive student behaviour; only three studies on mental health support; critical value of evaluating and publishing evidence from disability-inclusive TPD interventions
studies.latest_known: A corrigendum (DOI: 10.1002/cl2.1315) was published 25 February 2023 correcting the original article (DOI: 10.1002/cl2.1287, published 25 November 2022). The content of the correction is not publicly retrievable from search results. The draft itself acknowledges this correction exists but states it could not be read, while simultaneously drawing on the uncorrected article throughout the body text.
studies.what_changed: The corrigendum's specific corrections are unknown. Any figure or claim drawn from the original article — including the 50-study count, the 16-of-41-countries figure, and the qualitative country-level findings — may have been altered. The draft uses these figures in the body while disclaiming reliance on the source, which is internally inconsistent and leaves all Ahmed-sourced claims unverified against the corrected version.

studies.name: Saran, White & Kuper — Evidence and gap map of studies assessing the effectiveness of interventions for people with disabilities in LMICs
studies.draft_uses: Studies mostly target individual characteristics rather than structures; absence of evidence on what works to promote disability inclusion described as a very striking gap; most studies from upper-middle-income countries with limited evidence from low-income countries; more studies needed on all impairment types including visual and hearing
studies.latest_known: A corrigendum (DOI: 10.1002/cl2.1104) was published 12 July 2020, correcting the original article (DOI: 10.1002/cl2.1070, published 9 January 2020). The corrigendum changed the income-country breakdown: the original stated 'over half (n=49) the impact evaluations come from upper-middle income countries'; the corrected version reads 'almost half (n=50) the impact evaluations come from lower-middle income countries, closely followed by upper-middle income countries (n=48).' No further update to the EGM itself was found beyond this 2020 corrigendum. The draft acknowledges the correction exists but states it could not be read, while drawing on the source in the body text.
studies.what_changed: The corrigendum reverses the income-country finding: the draft's implicit framing that most studies come from upper-middle-income countries reflects the uncorrected text. The corrected version states that almost half come from lower-middle-income countries (n=50), closely followed by upper-middle income (n=48), with low-income countries still the notable gap (n=9). The draft sentence 'Most studies come from upper-middle-income countries, with limited evidence from low-income countries' is therefore drawn from the uncorrected article and does not match the corrected figures.

studies.latest_known: The protocol (Campbell Systematic Reviews, 17, e1197, published 23 October 2021) was formally superseded by the full review Hunt et al. 2025 (Campbell Systematic Reviews, 21, e70016). PubMed records this as 'Update in: Campbell Syst Rev. 2025 Feb 6;21(1):e70016.' The draft correctly treats [4] as a protocol and does not draw findings figures from it.
studies.what_changed: N/A — the draft uses [4] only for protocol-level background observations, not for outcome figures. The full review [1] that supersedes it is already the draft's primary source, so no stale figures arise from this citation.
